full_judgment: 29. Here, the question arises how, when and after following what procedure the concerned authority changed the RS Record of right from the name of the present plaintiff-opposite party in SA Record to the defendant-petitioner has not been mentioned anywhere in the record of the present case. It is true that the provision of law regarding burden of proof is the plaintiff has to prove its own case with the standard of balance of probability but the questions are whether the petitioners-Government produced any document in the courts to substantiate break of chain of title in order to change record of right and whether relevant government authorities have given any opportunity to the recorded owner to the suit land before changing the record of right from SA to RS? If it has not been done, it is apparent that plaintiff is not aware about the reason for such change. In my consideration burden of proof in the given circumstances is to be shifted from the plaintiff-opposite party to the defendant-petitioners who is the maker of the RS Record but there is nothing on record of this case as to the reason behind the change of the record of right from SA to RS in favour of the Government. I am sure that the relevant authority has not changed the record of right with a consideration to benefit the government rather it has been done randomly and without following any legal procedure for such change with a corrupt intention and such kind of silent corruptions are causing unnecessary huge number of litigations and sufferings to the holder of valid documents, thus, the laid administrative authorities should be held accountable.
